layers.note: A succulent mat on rock outcrops, ledges and gravel.

elevation_m.note: Montane to alpine in the Cascades and Olympics.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −12 to 2 °C; gone below −20 °C and above 6 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −32 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −40 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 8 to 18 °C; gone below 5 °C, where summers are too short, and above 22 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 700 to 3,500 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 400.

degree_days_5.note: About 200 to 1,900 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 80.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.45, gone by 0.3.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.5 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.7.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Spreading stonecrop grows from southern Alaska to Oregon in the coastal mountains and Cascades (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
